id_and_class.summary: Daniel Boyd argues that every information system, from computers to brains, works through non-physical informational entities built in hierarchical levels on top of physical states. Consciousness is one such emergent, non-material phenomenon generated by the brain, and it exerts top-down control over neuronal activity, making Boyd’s view a form of emergent dualism.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a high-level informational phenomenon, built from fundamental informational entities associated with neuronal states and residing in an ‘information dimension’ beyond the three physical ones.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mutual dependency: information exists only because of processes in its material substrate, yet high-level informational processes determine what happens in that substrate, as a running program determines bit states.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Strong emergence (each informational level has properties absent from the level below and exerts downward causation)
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Boyd does not specifically predict qualia, but holds that EIT predicts comparably significant transitions between fundamental informational entities and the high-level phenomena built from them.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Physical matter and energy, non-physical informational entities (such as binary values), hierarchical emergent informational structures, and an additional information dimension.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: In computers, through coding protocols that let us build and read back informational levels. In brains, which self-organize without a code, high-level information cannot be reconstructed from neural measurements, so evidence is indirect and includes our own experience.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Hierarchical levels of information, like bits, bytes, subroutines, and programs in a computer, built in the brain from informational entities tied to neuronal states.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal; mental causation; free will; non-conscious mental functions
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Informational emergence with downward causation: high-level informational processes determine the states of the physical substrate that carries them.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Informational levels are built up hierarchically. In programmed computers this happens by coded design; in neural networks it happens through self-organization.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Not located in physical space; Boyd places informational phenomena in an additional information dimension, associated with the brain’s neuronal states.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Non-physical mental activity determines the physical activity of neurons and so controls behavior. Physical determinism is incomplete, and causal closure must include informational phenomena.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: A physical state such as a magnetic polarity carries a binary value that no physical device can read directly; its meaning comes from the system’s design. Higher levels are built by altering bit sequences according to strict coding protocols.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Systems that evolved or were designed to work by information all depend on the causal influence of non-physical informational entities.
core_claims_and_evidence: Binary values in computers are tied to physical states but are not made of matter or energy.
Each level of informational organization has properties that do not exist at the level beneath it.
High-level informational processes determine the physical states of their substrate, so physical determinism is incomplete.
The association of neural states with informational entities explains both neural correlates of consciousness and why consciousness cannot be found by examining neural activity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Theoretical argument by analogy with programmed computers, supported indirectly by the reality of subjective experience

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Treating binary values and software as non-physical is disputed: most computer scientists regard information as a physical pattern under an interpretation. Boyd acknowledges that, because brains self-organize without a code, their informational level cannot be read from neural data, which makes the theory hard to test.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Why only some informational systems are conscious, and what the information dimension consists of, are not specified.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Boyd presents EIT as dualist yet places consciousness in the same family as software, which sits uneasily with the more common view that software is physical.

AI_consciousness.rationale: EIT treats artificial neural networks as emergent information systems like brains, but Boyd holds that only biological self-organization is known to produce consciousness.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since informational phenomena exist only because of processes in their material substrate, the mind should not outlast the brain that generates it.

virtual_immortality.rationale: A brain’s high-level informational phenomena cannot be reconstructed from measurable neuronal states, which blocks reading out a mind for copying.
